_source: Every quotation and figure below is taken verbatim from 'Portraits of Change: Mixed Reality Music Recital Research Portfolio' (Thomas Graves, 11/28/21, updated 2022). Hues, running minutes and stage-light RGB are Appendix B. MIDI assignments are Appendix B. Stage plots are Appendix C. Spelling is the source's own and is not corrected.

performance.title: Portraits of Change
performance.subtitle: a Mixed Reality Music Recital
performance.lede: Using these new technologies, we can present musical portraits painted in real-time with the live music driving every visual change.

portraits.title: Trumpet Concerto in E-flat Major — I. Allegro
portraits.note: Instead of sculpting busts of heads on stage or making literal 2D portraits, these song environments represent a combination of visual art and aural art in a real-time performance to capture the feeling of the music and its composer.

portraits.title: Sonata for Trumpet and Piano, op. 137 — I. Mit Kraft
portraits.note: In this performance, the piano creates an environmental visual effect all around the trumpet player and the audience. The back and forth between the two can be felt spatially through both aural and visual senses.

portraits.title: Music for the Royal Fireworks — IV. La Rejouissance
portraits.players: Thomas Graves, Ivan Acurio, Ray Beltran, Richard Platt, Tyler Perea
portraits.note: This piece originally for wind instruments could be considered an early audiovisual music performance.

portraits.title: “Dear Theodosia,” from Hamilton
portraits.players: Thomas Graves, Tyler Perea, Ivan Acurio, Richard Platt, Ray Beltran
portraits.note: a brass quintet is used with the two trumpets representing Aaron Burr and Alexander Hamilton.

portraits.title: West End Blues
portraits.players: Thomas Graves, Tony Szajowski, Jay Martinez, Michael Manzanares
portraits.note: We tune the chromatic circle so that blue will be on Eb, the tonic of this particular Blues.

portraits.title: All Limbs Are, from 12 Little Spells
portraits.players: Thomas Graves, Tony Szajowski, Jay Martinez
portraits.note: By applying a two-color palette on each alternating note, we can show these chromatic and whole tone movements in a visually appealing way by using complimentary colors.

portraits.title: Donna Lee
portraits.players: Thomas Graves, Tony Szajowski, Jordan Barney, Connor Thomas, Michael Manzanares
portraits.note: The goal of using chromatic color wheels around a chromatic music circle is to allow visual communication of the chord changes and improvisation patterns as they emerge sonically to the audience.

portraits.title: La Vie en rose
portraits.players: Thomas Graves, Jordan Barney, DJ Henson, Tony Szajowski, Michael Manzanares
portraits.note: Our arrangement digs into the ‘happy hues’ near red and blue.

portraits.title: Bitches Brew
portraits.players: Thomas Graves, Tony Szajowski, Jay Martinez, Jordan Barney, Thaddeus Zimmerman, DJ Henson, Michael Manzanares
portraits.note: With this song, we are telling the story of the origins of the universe. Why? Because what signifies chaos and searching for meaning more than cosmology!
portraits.rigNote: Appendix B lists every instrument in this piece as environmental. The stage plot for the same piece marks the trumpet, bass, e-kit and bass clarinet as tracked. Both are reproduced as drawn.

portraits.title: Resolution, from A Love Supreme
portraits.composer: John Coltrane; lyrics by Kurt Elling, arr. Bob Mintzer
portraits.players: Thomas Graves, CSU-Pueblo Jazz Ensemble I
portraits.note: Visually, constellations will float in the air while a story about beginnings is unfolded through the improvised melodies of Coltrane backed by the live big band.

key.def: Indicates which MIDI channel this specific mic’d instrument will be controlling.
Tracked instrument with Vive Tracker either attached to instrument, near it, or mounted on a mic stand.
Environmental effects will be used without the need for a tracker but will still need a phantom-powered microphone to go through the MIDI conversion system.
